Reproduce the dashboard's force ranking as an editable plot

Source: R/plot.R
btg_plot_disparity.Rd

Recreates the values, eligibility rule and ordering of the dashboard's ranking of forces by the rate at which one group is stopped compared with White residents. This is a static ggplot version: interactive hover text and previous-year change annotations are not reproduced. Partial reporting is labelled explicitly, each bar carries its 95% interval, and one force can be highlighted as the dashboard's selected force.

Usage

btg_plot_disparity(
  x = btg_get_data(),
  n = 10L,
  ranking = c("highest", "lowest", "closest"),
  year = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  highlight = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A dataset from btg_get_data(): force_disparity (2025, Black) or force_ethnicity_year (any year and group it holds).

n

Maximum number of displayed forces, from 1 to 44.

ranking

One of "highest", "lowest", or "closest" to parity.

year

The calendar year to draw. NULL draws the latest year the source covers in full, which is the dashboard's starting year.

group

The group compared with White: "Black", "Asian", "Mixed" or "Other". NULL draws Black.

highlight

Optional Police.uk identifier of one force to draw in the selected-force colour, as the dashboard does for its chosen force.

Value

An editable ggplot with a saved evidence specification. The underlying original chart table is available with btg_figure_data().

Details

Ranks refer to every eligible force in that year and group, even after selecting forces. The solid line is parity (1). An asterisk and a lighter fill mark incomplete or unverified monthly returns; the dashboard verifies submissions only inside a recent window, so earlier years show every force as unverified; when that is true of every displayed force the bars keep the ordinary fill and the caption says so. A highlighted force is drawn only if it falls within the n displayed forces, as on the dashboard. Counts are not annualised. Display eligibility does not imply complete or comparable exposure, or establish discrimination.

Examples

p <- btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data())
p
